findings.title: Failure-path message is an Error object at the controller send boundary despite its string declaration
findings.evidence: Independent verification against the supplied raw target confirms the source-level send-argument mismatch, with the original medium severity preserved. Ordered trace: MongoDBClient.findOneById forwards the callback's error unchanged (target/src/modules/database/services/service.mongo.db.client.ts:42-46); StoreUser.get rejects it unchanged (target/src/modules/users/services/stores/store.user.ts:50-59); ServiceUser.find catches it and passes it as the second argument of ResponseFailure (target/src/modules/users/services/service.user.ts:81-98); ResponseFailure stores that value directly in response.message alongside code and error (target/src/modules/common/utils/response.ts:52-58); ControllerUser.find reads resp.code for status and sends resp unchanged (target/src/servers/sample.typescrit.swagger.api/controllers/controller.user.ts:47-67). No persistent storage or queue exists on this response path. IModelResponse has only declared fields and no initializer, constructor, getter or toJSON (target/src/modules/interfaces/api/i.model.response.ts:1-6). Extracted execution captures exactly own fields [code,error,message] with message the identical native Error. The far-side source contract selected for 500 is UserErrorResponse (controller.user.ts:29-46): its decorated fields are code:number (required), message:string (optional), error:string (required); data:any is declared but undecorated (target/src/modules/users/models/user.ts:27-48). Optional message does not allow an object when present. The local ECMAScript JSON.stringify experiment emits precisely top-level [code,error,message], nested message fields [], and no data. Error.message is never read/extracted on this path; it is non-enumerable on the injected native Error. The field-name sets otherwise match the decorated source contract; no actual client reader was supplied, so no field written-but-unread or client reads-but-never-sent finding is established. Actual serializer boundary: controller invokes Express send(object); the Express serializer implementation is outside the supplied target, so actual HTTP field enumeration remains unavailable. Swagger UI loads /api-docs/swagger.json (target/swagger/index.html:77-89), but generated Swagger JSON and a consumer are unavailable. Therefore generated-schema validation, HTTP bytes and SDK rejection are not independently confirmed. Refutation attempts: string-control failure traverses the same extracted chain and conforms; thus this is conditional on a non-string error, not every failure. No normalization exists in the traced response path; TypeScript annotations do not coerce values. Exact pinned file hashes, extraction line spans, assumptions and observed output are retained in review/verifier-reproduction.json; executable first-party reproduction is review/verifier-reproduction.mjs. The script checks all seven target file SHA256 pins before evaluating any isolated method; it loads no application constructors or configuration. Safe recommended disposition: map failures to a stable public string (and optionally a deliberately specified public error code), while logging internal diagnostic details privately; never automatically return raw internal exception messages.
findings.counterexample: Run node review/verifier-reproduction.mjs from the pinned research directory (or pass its absolute target directory). With the Mongo callback injected with new Error('offline database failure'), the actual extracted callback/store/service/response/controller methods call the response mock with status 500 and message identical to that Error, whereas UserErrorResponse.message declares string. Observed separate JSON.stringify output is {"code":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":{}}. Control input 'public safe message' emits {"code":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","message":"public safe message"} and satisfies the declared message type. Exit status 0 on Node v22.23.3. This confirms only extracted source behavior and local ECMAScript serialization, not actual Express HTTP bytes, generated Swagger behavior, a client failure, or a production exploit.

limitations: Read only mechanically filtered claims, raw target, and public review protocol/contracts; no finder report, parent rationale, prior reproduction, or peer report read.
Bounded scope: POST /user/find/userId and UserErrorResponse plus its direct failure-value chain. No repository-wide or diff review.
No dependency installation, server/network/database calls, credentials, or real client runtime used. Unrelated constructors/config were not evaluated; no credentials copied.

Reproduction strips only TypeScript signatures/type arguments and supplies an empty runtime equivalent of the declaration-only IModelResponse class, plus offline ObjectID/JWT/telemetry/DB/response stubs. It is not a compiled integration test.

The actual Express serializer, generated Swagger JSON and final client consumer are not available in supplied raw target. Actual wire field list and SDK/schema-validator rejection remain unverified; no deployed failure or exploit is claimed.

The 400 validation.error/Joi-object path is source-supported at target/src/modules/common/utils/validation.ts:44-59 but not executed with real Joi and not independently confirmed. Candidate secondary claims remain bounded by this limitation.
Native Error prototype/serialization behavior measured on Node v22.23.3. Historic deployed runtime and externally patched Error prototypes were not reproduced.
